blocks.text: Peel the thin transparent skin from an onion bulb, place it in a drop of water under a microscope, and you will see hundreds of neat brick-shaped boxes. Every yam tuber, every mango leaf and every drop of your own blood is built from boxes like these. They are cells, and everything alive is made of them.

blocks.markdown:
## The cell theory

Biology rests on three statements known as the **cell theory**:

1. All living organisms are made of one or more cells.
2. The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.
3. All cells arise from pre-existing cells by division.

A cell is small — a typical animal cell is about 20 micrometres across, so about fifty of them side by side would span one millimetre. Being small keeps the **surface area to volume ratio** high, so materials can diffuse in and out fast enough to keep the cell alive.

blocks.title: Organelle
blocks.text: A specialised structure inside a cell that carries out a particular job, in the same way that different rooms in a hospital carry out different jobs. The cytoplasm holds the organelles in place and is where many reactions occur.

blocks.markdown:
### Picturing a cell without a diagram

Imagine an animal cell as a soft, flexible bag. The **cell membrane** is the bag itself: thin, and selective about what passes through. Inside, filling most of the space, is the jelly-like **cytoplasm**. Suspended near the centre sits the **nucleus**, a round body with its own double membrane and a dark central spot called the nucleolus. Scattered through the cytoplasm are sausage-shaped **mitochondria**, tiny dot-like **ribosomes** (many stuck to a folded sheet of membranes called the endoplasmic reticulum), a stack of flattened sacs called the **Golgi apparatus**, and small spherical **lysosomes**.

A plant cell is different in three obvious ways. It has a rigid **cell wall** outside the membrane, giving it a fixed rectangular shape. It has one very large central **vacuole** filled with sap, which pushes the cytoplasm into a thin layer against the wall. And in the cytoplasm are green disc-shaped **chloroplasts**.

blocks.markdown:
### Prokaryotes and eukaryotes

Bacteria are **prokaryotic**: they have no true nucleus, no mitochondria and no membrane-bound organelles. Their DNA is a single circular loop lying free in the cytoplasm, and their cell wall is not made of cellulose.

Plants, animals, fungi and protists are **eukaryotic**: their DNA is enclosed in a nucleus and they contain membrane-bound organelles. Prokaryotic cells are also much smaller, typically 1–5 micrometres.

blocks.title: Identifying a cell from a description
blocks.prompt: Under the microscope a student sees a cell with a rigid rectangular outline, a large clear space occupying most of the middle, and green discs pressed against the outer edge. There is no visible centriole. What kind of cell is it, and which organelle carries out photosynthesis?

steps.text: The rigid rectangular outline means a cell wall is present. Only plant cells have a cellulose cell wall, so the cell is not an animal cell.
The large clear space in the middle is the permanent central sap vacuole, which is another plant feature.
The green discs are chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll. Chlorophyll traps light energy, so this is where photosynthesis happens.
The absence of a centriole is consistent with a higher plant cell, confirming the identification.

blocks.answer: It is a plant cell (from a green part of the plant), and photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts.

items: Cells with many mitochondria are cells that use a lot of energy — muscle cells, sperm cells and the cells lining the kidney tubule.
Cells that make and export a lot of protein, such as those in the pancreas, are packed with ribosomes, rough ER and Golgi bodies.
Red blood cells lose their nucleus so they can carry more haemoglobin.
Root hair cells have no chloroplasts because no light reaches them underground.

blocks.title: WAEC and JAMB tip
blocks.text: Examiners love the words 'partially permeable' for the cell membrane and 'fully permeable' for the cell wall. Do not write 'semi-permeable membrane' for the cell wall — the wall lets almost everything through and only the membrane is selective.

points: All organisms are made of cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure and function.
The nucleus controls the cell, mitochondria release energy, ribosomes make protein and the Golgi apparatus packages it.
Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole; animal cells do not.
The cell membrane is partially permeable and controls entry and exit; the cell wall is fully permeable and gives support.
Prokaryotes such as bacteria lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotes have both.
